Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zufapmx 0.0.0.9000

  • Models follow one rule for who may assign and read what (design D18): parameters, random effects, compartments and time are never assigned, ODE code does not reassign individual parameters, and individual statements do not read compartment amounts. The rxode2 reader moves statements into the ODE code until that holds, and keeps an endpoint that other statements read as a statement.

  • Readers refuse more constructs that would change predictions: a Y reassigned or set inside IF, a scale or dosing attribute assigned twice, TSCALE, XSCALE, INITIALOFF, code after a plain ELSE, fractional compartment indices, $ODE beside $PKMODEL, time from the wrong record (TIME in $DES, SOLVERTIME outside $ODE), $NMXML and $NMEXT options the reader does not honour, C++ integer division of comparisons, and rxode2’s combined1().

  • A NONMEM Y that does not use F, as in IPRED = A(2)/V, gives its own prediction instead of the compartment amount.

  • A refusal of a statement points at its record’s first line, and a writer’s refusal lists only formats that do write the model.

  • pmx_write_nonmem() lists the model’s covariates in $INPUT. Writers record lost bounds on residual standard deviations, and pmx_read_mrgsolve() records $PARAM values written as expressions.

  • pmx_read_rxode2() accepts = in ini() and combined2().

  • An invalid argument is a zufapmx_model_error with one wording across functions, and a model edited after reading is validated again before it is written or inspected.

  • Fidelity is stricter: a write is "equivalent" only through the reparameterisations writers are known to make, and a translation that reads back as a different model is a zufapmx_write_error.

  • Time is one symbol, t, read from and written to each format’s own spelling (NONMEM TIME/T, mrgsolve TIME/SOLVERTIME, rxode2 t/time). Free names are recorded as covariates in a model’s provenance.

  • Readers refuse more of what they cannot translate faithfully (dosing assignments inside IF, undeclared THETA/ETA/EPS, C++ integer division) and accept more of what they can ($PKMODEL over $PARAM, $SIZES, record options, statement-defined residual parameters).

  • pmx_read_mrgsolve() reads an mrgsolve model file and pmx_write_mrgsolve() writes one.

  • pmx_write_nonmem() writes a NONMEM control stream.

  • pmx_read_nonmem() reads a NONMEM control stream, with final estimates from run.xml, the .ext file or the .lst report.

  • pmx_read_rxode2() reads an rxode2 or nlmixr2 model function and pmx_write_rxode2() writes one. pmx_fidelity() and pmx_losses() say how faithful a written model is.

  • pmx_parameters(), pmx_omega() and pmx_ode() inspect a model, and print() summarises it.

  • zufapmx_corpus() lists the shipped model corpus: one-, two- and three-compartment closed-form models and a Michaelis-Menten ODE model, each written in NONMEM, rxode2 and mrgsolve form with its typical-subject predictions.

  • Initial CRAN submission.

Developed by Pedro Baltazar.
